notes: No selective or additional licensing. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies (5 or more people, 2 or more households). Fees run £664 to £882 and the council's public register covers mandatory licences only.
research: PRIMARY SOURCES READ IN FULL, all council-owned. (1) The live HMO page states the licensing trigger as 'A property rented to 5 or more people who form more than 1 household' where 'some or all tenants share toilet, bathroom or kitchen facilities' - the national mandatory threshold, with no designation, wards or dates. (2) FEE SCHEDULE, mandatory bands only: 5-6 bed spaces £664; 7-8 £764; 9+ £882; 'A licence will normally last for a maximum of five years'. No selective or additional fee line, which a live scheme would need to be enforceable. (3) The statutory public register says 'Kirklees Council keeps a register of all licences that have been issued to operate Houses in Multiple Occupation' and scopes it to properties let to '5 or more separate tenants not in the same family group'. A discretionary scheme would require its own register entries. (4) The full housing index was enumerated link by link: HMO, HMO register, landlord accreditation, guide to renting privately, Renters' Rights Act, report repairs. No discretionary licensing page. (5) The Private Sector Housing Assistance Policy (October 2025) was read in full and contains no selective or additional licensing provision. (6) A search of democracy.kirklees.gov.uk for 'selective licensing' returned no results, so no cabinet or committee report proposes a scheme. TRAPS: a legacy landlord booklet carries headed sections 'Additional licensing of HMOs' and 'Selective licensing' that look like announcements but are generic 2006-era recitals of the statutory powers, and the same document concludes 'Kirklees Council, initially intends to implement mandatory licensing and to continue to work with landlords... through the accreditation scheme.' Aggregators also publish a 'Selective licensing in Kirklees: streets, fees, postcode check' page, which is not a council source. ON THE DEPRIVATION POINT: Kirklees plainly has areas that would support a case for selective licensing, but the council has not made one; its published choice is accreditation plus enforcement.

notes: No selective or additional licensing. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies (5 or more people, 2 or more households). The 2026-27 fee list carries mandatory HMO fees only, from £875 for a five-year licence.
research: PRIMARY SOURCES READ IN FULL, all council-owned. (1) The council's own licence-need test states: 'A landlord must have a licence for a privately rented HMO if the property being rented out: is occupied by five or more people; those people form two or more households; tenants share some amenities like kitchen, bathroom or laundry'. That is the national mandatory threshold and nothing beyond it. If a selective scheme were designated, ordinary private rented homes in the designated area would need a licence and this page could not be written that way. (2) FEE SCHEDULE 2026-2027, mandatory HMO only: five-year licences £875 (5 persons) rising to £1,880 (16+ persons); one-year £420 to £731; plus accommodation certificate and Part 1 enforcement at full cost recovery. No discretionary licensing fee. (3) The housing index enumerated in full: empty homes, energy efficiency, homelessness, Homes for Ukraine, HMO, housing strategies, housing support, Renters' Rights Act, TESS. No discretionary licensing page. (4) The council's complete licence register enumerates taxi and private hire, animal, leisure and personal treatment, business and street trading, gambling, child employment, and alcohol and entertainment, with no housing licence at all. (5) The A-Z was pulled for letters S and L: no selective licensing entry and no landlord licensing entry. TWO TRAPS, both material here: (a) the landlord guidance page carries the passages 'Additional licencing of HMOs is a discretionary power that Councils may decide to apply...' and 'This is where the Council may declare that certain areas, for example, where there is low demand for housing and/or antisocial behaviour, are appropriate for selective licencing.' Conditional recitals of the statutory powers, with no area, dates or fee. (b) The customer portal hosts a 'Selective Licensing' presentation given to the Private Landlord Forum in July 2013 and consultation material from November 2012, including survey findings. That is a historic consultation that did not result in a designation. ON THE DEPRIVATION POINT: Knowsley did actively explore selective licensing in 2012-13 and did not proceed, which is consistent with the negative finding.

notes: Lancaster consulted in 2023 on landlord licensing in Morecambe's West End, but Cabinet resolved on 16 April 2024 not to implement it, choosing targeted enforcement instead. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies.
research: The highest-risk council in this batch, settled on the official minutes rather than a secondary report. PRIMARY SOURCE, the statutory record: Cabinet minutes of 16 April 2024, published 18 April 2024, effective 26 April 2024. Minute 99, 'Review of the Consultation on Landlord Licensing and the enforcement of housing standards in the West End of Morecambe', set out three options: 'Option 1: Do nothing'; 'Option 2: Introduce a selective landlord licensing scheme in the West End of Morecambe'; 'Option 3: Update an alternative enforcement approach, build on landlord and tenant engagement and explore the introduction of a Good Landlord Charter.' The minutes record 'The officer preferred option is option 3'. On a recorded vote of 8 to 1, Cabinet RESOLVED: '(1) That Cabinet notes the outcome of the public consultation... (2) That Cabinet agrees to not implementing landlord licensing at this time from this consultation, but to concentrate on a more intelligence led, targeted enforcement approach. (3) That approval be given to co-develop and agree to the introduction of a Good Landlords Charter. (4) That Cabinet agrees to the commissioning of a full stock condition survey... (5) That approval be given to the development of an action plan...' Option 2 was rejected and no designation was made. CORROBORATION: the Private Landlords Newsletter fifth edition (July 2023) confirms the consultation covered 'the West End and Heysham North areas of Morecambe', notes 'A previous consultation for a selective and additional licensing scheme was held in 2017 where the decision was to pause implementation... in favour of a targeted enforcement approach', and states plainly under 'Current property licensing schemes in Lancaster District': 'Lancaster City Council operates the mandatory licensing scheme as this is the national scheme required by the Housing Act 2004.' The seventh edition (May 2024) reports the same decision to landlords. FEE SCHEDULE from April 2026, read in full: new five-year licence £156 application plus £602 licence, £758 total for a five person HMO, plus £57 per extra person; renewal £654; maximum £1,600; £114 discount for accredited landlords. Mandatory only, no discretionary line. The private rented accommodation index lists ten sub-pages with no licensing scheme page; /selective-licensing returns 404. Recorded as no scheme rather than 'proposed' because the consultation closed and was refused. NOTE the wording 'at this time from this consultation' leaves the door open, so Lancaster is worth re-checking. Historic: Cabinet on 8 August 2017 had approved developing a Morecambe scheme and consulting, which was then paused.

notes: No selective or additional licensing. The council confirmed in an FOI response 'just the mandatory scheme' and that additional or selective licensing 'is not required in LDC'. The 2026-27 fee schedule lists mandatory HMO fees only.
research: Backed by a direct council statement. The published FOI response (FOI 14362 'Mandatory HMO') answers whether the council 'only has the Mandatory HMO licensing scheme in place at this current time'. Under 'Response by Lewes District Council' it says: 'Yes, just the mandatory scheme' and 'Additional or selective licensing is not required in LDC, therefore no consultations were carried out. LDC has a very small number of HMO's'. Asked for 'any live and up and coming designations and with a map of coverage area', the answer is 'N/A'. CURRENCY CHECK, since the FOI is not recent: the HMO page (last modified 13 May 2026) offers a single licence route covering 'HMO's in Eastbourne borough and the Lewes district'. The 'HMO License Fee Schedule 2026-2027' was read in full: Shared House 5 persons £1,140 new and £799 renewal, rising to £1,213 at 9 persons; Bedsit £1,283 to £1,573; Hostel £1,140 up to £2,943 for 81+ persons; plus immigration inspection £150, pre-application advice £185, missed appointment £100, unlicensed HMO inspection £350, paper form £50, late application £50. It confirms 'As shared houses are licensed for 5 or more occupants' and frames refunds solely around 'a licence under Part 2 of the Housing Act 2004'. A text search of the whole PDF for 'selective', 'additional licen', 'part 3', 's.56' and 'designat' returned zero matches. THREE TRAPS on this shared site, all avoided: (1) a news item 'Council takes action to limit HMO conversions' is EASTBOURNE Borough, and is an Article 4 planning Direction covering 'Devonshire, Meads and Upperton wards, and a small part of St Anthony's ward' from 30 July. Named wards plus a hard date make it look exactly like a designation; it is neither licensing nor Lewes. (2) Pages titled 'Selective area housing licences - 1350' and 'Selective housing areas - 1349' rank top on the council's own search but are records-retention schedule entries carrying 'Retention Period Years 6' and 'Legislation Name: Limitation Act 1980 (Section 2)'. This boilerplate appears on many council sites regardless of any scheme. (3) The shared democracy site's HMO papers are Eastbourne's, not Lewes'. Exact-phrase searches returned 7 hits for 'selective licensing' and 14 for 'additional licensing', every one being that boilerplate, the FOI itself, Eastbourne planning material, Licensing Act 2003 policy, or the title of the HMO Management Regulations 2007.

notes: No selective or additional licensing. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies (5 or more people, 2 or more families), fee £850 plus £75 per bedroom above five. A 2025-26 delivery plan lists researching a scheme as 'Not started'.
research: The HMO licence page states the trigger as mandatory only: 'If you are the owner/manager of a house in multiple occupation (HMO) that is rented out to five or more people, who form two or more families, and who share facilities such as a bathroom, kitchen, sink or toilet, you must get an HMO licence.' FEE SCHEDULE, HMO lines only: 'Licence fee £850'; 'Plus cost per bedroom above 5 £75', capped at £5,000; 'Renewal licence fee £850'; 'HMO immigration inspection £220'. No discretionary licensing fee line. The licensing index enumerates alcohol and event, street trading, animal, taxi, pavement, gambling, charitable collections, sex shop, caravan and residential site, scrap metal and special treatments plus HMO, with no discretionary housing scheme. A crawl of 295 housing and licensing pages found zero occurrences of the word 'selective' anywhere, and zero occurrences of 'additional licensing' used as a scheme. TWO TRAPS, both material: (1) MODEL-FORM BOILERPLATE. The downloadable HMO application form (June 2019) carries the line 'ONLY COMPLETE THIS APPLICATION FORM FOR A LICENSABLE HOUSE IN MULTIPLE OCCUPATION, WHICH INCLUDES MANDATORY LICENSING AND ADDITIONAL LICENSING.' Standard national model-form wording covering both regimes; there is no designation notice, coverage area, dates or additional licensing fee. (2) PROPOSAL-STAGE WORDING. The 'Housing, homelessness and rough sleeping delivery plan 2025-2026' contains the action 'Research benefits of additional/selective licensing approach for particular neighbourhoods and adopt if need arises', status 'Not started'. Aspiration, not a consultation and not a designation, so no 'proposed' scheme is recorded. It is a genuine forward signal though: of these twelve, Lichfield is the most likely to designate in future. LIMITATION: the site IP-blocked automated access partway through, so the sweep covered housing, licensing, homelessness, environmental health and community sections rather than all 4,013 URLs; committee papers were not inspected.

notes: No selective or additional licensing. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies (5 or more people). Lincoln does have a city-wide Article 4 Direction from 1 March 2016, but that is planning permission for HMO conversion, not a licence.
research: PRIMARY SOURCES READ IN FULL, which matters because Lincoln is a student city where additional licensing would be unsurprising. (1) The HMO page states 'An HMO must have a licence if it is occupied by 5 or more people' - the national mandatory threshold, with no lower threshold and no designated area. (2) FEE SCHEDULE, the decisive document: 'Government regulations came into force in October 2018 that require Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs) with five or more tenants to be licensed by the council'; 'Basic fee (up to 5 bedrooms) New application £1470'; renewal £1270; '6 to 10 bedrooms - Basic fee + 10%'; '11 to 15 bedrooms - Basic fee + 20%'; '16 to 20 bedrooms - Basic fee + 30%'; Trusted Landlord Scheme discount £100; 60 per cent payable on application and 40 per cent on grant. One fee structure, tied to the mandatory regime. An additional licensing scheme covering small student HMOs, the scheme type one would expect here, would require its own fee line and there is none. (3) The HMO section index contains exactly three items: Complying with the Law, HMO Article 4 Formal Process, and Houses in Multiple Occupation. (4) The Private Housing index lists ten items with no discretionary licensing page. (5) The landlord compliance page covers tenancy agreements, EPCs, gas safety, deposit protection and electrical safety, imposing no licensing obligation beyond the mandatory regime. THREE TRAPS: (a) THE BIG ONE. Lincoln operates a city-wide Article 4 Direction: 'On 1st March 2016 the City of Lincoln Council introduced an Article 4 Direction' removing permitted development rights for 'the change of use from a use falling within Class C3 (dwelling houses)... to a use falling within Class C4 (houses in multiple occupation)' across 'the City of Lincoln'. It has a commencement date and district-wide coverage and is frequently mistaken for licensing. Planning control, never a scheme. (b) The council's 'Mandatory Licensing of Houses in Multiple Occupation' document recites 'Offences in relation to the Selective Licensing of houses [s95 Housing Act...]' inside a boilerplate list of civil penalty offences. (c) NAME COLLISION, and it is severe: North East Lincolnshire Council and North Lincolnshire Council both run genuine selective licensing schemes and dominate search results for 'Lincoln selective licensing', while Boston Borough Council launched a consultation on a town-wide additional licensing scheme in March 2026. All three are separate Lincolnshire authorities and none is City of Lincoln.

notes: No selective or additional licensing. Cabinet considered additional licensing for smaller HMOs and declined it on 19 March 2025, stating officers 'remain of this opinion' that existing enforcement powers are adequate.
research: Independently verified twice, by two separate research passes reaching the same primary document. Maidstone actively considered additional licensing and declined it. The Cabinet decision 'Houses in Multiple Occupation Proposals', 19 March 2025, records: 'MBC has previously considered creating an Additional Licensing Scheme for smaller HMOs (of 4 persons or less), but its Housing Standards Team have felt that existing enforcement powers (through Housing Standards, Community Safety and Environmental Health) are adequate to address any issues. They remain of this opinion.' It adds that 'it would be prudent to see how this Bill progresses as it will deliver additional powers over rented properties, so allowing the Council to continue to focus licencing on larger HMOs.' The resolutions adopted were to pursue an HMO Supplementary Planning Document and to review the W1, W2 and W4 Controlled Residents Parking Zones. No scheme was designated and selective licensing was never proposed. The live HMO page gives mandatory criteria only, at least five people not all one household sharing facilities, and a single fee: 'The total cost of the application is £930. For accredited landlords, it's £895.' The Housing Strategy refers only to the statutory regime: 'We are active in ensuring those HMOs that fall within the statutory licensing scheme meet the requirements of the regulations.' A crawl of all 875 reachable pages found zero occurrences of 'selective licensing' or 'additional licensing'; 27 pages returned a JavaScript challenge and were checked individually, none licensing-related. TRAP: the same Cabinet paper expresses a desire for an Article 4 Direction for HMOs and gives ward-level HMO concentrations (High Street 167, Fant and Oakwood 129). Planning and statistical, not designations, and the resulting SPD and parking zones name specific areas without being licensing. Because the March 2025 decision was a settled refusal rather than a live consultation, no 'proposed' scheme is recorded.

notes: No selective or additional licensing. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies. The council states plainly that an HMO occupied by 3 or 4 unrelated people is not licensable, and the 2026-27 fee list has one housing line, £1,099 new.
research: Maldon gives the clearest negative wording in the batch. The HMO service page states: 'You are required to obtain a licence from this Authority if the property is: rented to five or more people who form more than one household; and tenants share toilet, bathroom or kitchen facilities.' It then says explicitly: 'Please note an HMO occupied by 3 or 4 unrelated individuals is not licensable because fewer than 5 persons reside at the property. There are still legal requirements applicable to such properties.' That sentence is decisive. Additional licensing is precisely the mechanism that makes small HMOs of 3 or 4 occupants licensable, so a council cannot say they are not licensable while operating one; and selective licensing would extend licensing further still, to ordinary private rented homes. Both are excluded by the council's own words. FEE SCHEDULE, 'Environmental Fees from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027': across the entire schedule there is exactly ONE housing licence line, 'House in Multiple Occupation (HMO) | Up to 5 habitable rooms | Per extra room - New £1,099 Renewal £758 £61'. Every other line is animal, food, piercing, sex establishment, caravan and camping, private water or scrap metal. STRUCTURAL CORROBORATION: the complete A-Z of council services was enumerated across all 26 letters, 212 services. It contains exactly one housing licence, 'Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMO) Licence'. There is no entry under S for selective licensing and none under L or A for additional or landlord licensing. The public register is described as 'Properties that are currently licensed with the Maldon District Council', with no separate discretionary register, and licences are 'valid for 5 years'. The Essex-wide approved Code of Practice and Essex HMO Amenity Standards are a county collaboration on standards, not a designation. TRAP: searches for Maldon HMO licensing surface Epping Forest, Chelmsford and Colchester documents; separate Essex authorities, not used as evidence.

notes: No selective or additional licensing. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies. The 2026-27 fee table lists mandatory HMO fees only, from £893, and the council's licensing index contains no housing licence.
research: The HMO page describes an HMO as a property where 'at least 3 tenants live there, forming more than one household' sharing facilities, and states the licensing requirement arises where 'you rent a property to five or more people, not from the same household' - the national mandatory threshold. No designation, ward list or scheme wording appears. FEE SCHEDULE 2026-2027, published on the HMO page, mandatory lines only: standard licence single application £893.00 and multiple £764.00; increased occupancy 11-15 £1,454.00 / £1,387.00; 16-20 £1,454.00 / £1,387.00; 21+ £1,662.00 / £1,598.00; renewal single £653.00 and multiple £587.00, rising by band to £1,485.00 / £1,419.00. No discretionary licensing fee anywhere in the table. CORROBORATION: the Licensing index enumerates every licence type the council administers - Alcohol and Entertainment, Lotteries and Gambling, Taxis and Private Hire, Street Trading, Charitable Collections, Busking, Skin Piercing, Animal Licences, Sex Establishments, Scrap Metal, Caravan Site Licence, Pavement Licences - and contains no housing licence. The housing index lists only HMO, caravan licensing, empty homes and the Empty Homes Hub. The all-services index has no discretionary licensing entry. SHARED SERVICE NOTE: Malvern Hills shares services with Wychavon under South Worcestershire, but the HMO page gives Malvern Hills' own Private Sector Housing Team contact and Wychavon is a separate designating authority in any case. LIMITATION: the site search is JavaScript-driven and ignores URL query parameters, returning 'Results: 0' regardless of the term, so a site-search negative could not be obtained and was correctly not treated as evidence; committee papers were not inspected.

notes: No selective or additional licensing. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies (5 or more occupants, more than two households). The 2026-27 fees are £669 plus £334 in two parts, with no discretionary scheme fee.
research: Note the correct domain is melton.gov.uk; meltonbc.gov.uk does not resolve. The HMO page states: 'If you are a landlord or manager of a HMO will be required to hold a licence if the property has: Five or more occupants. More than two households.' The national mandatory threshold and nothing further; no designated area, ward, street or date. FEE SCHEDULE 2026-2027 under 'First Application', mandatory only: 'Application part 1 £669'; 'Application part 2 £334'; renewal Part 1 £508 and Part 2 £254; late payment £145; additional charge per room over five £28; HMO licensing advice £270 plus VAT; paper copies £36; Housing Act Notice Service £328; work in default £71 per hour. No discretionary licensing fee. CORROBORATION: the Licensing index lists alcohol and entertainment, animal, taxi, campsite, caravan site, pavement, pleasure boat, scrap metal, street trading, hairdresser and tattoo registrations, hypnotism, gambling and charitable collections, with no housing licensing. 'Advice for landlords' links only to HMO, fire safety, Universal Credit payments and the Renters' Rights Act. The strategies index lists housing strategies with no licensing designation. notes: No selective or additional licensing. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies, from 1 April 2018 for properties with 5 or more occupants. The 2026-27 fee schedule lists mandatory HMO fees only, from £1,083.
research: The HMO page states that from 1 April 2018 licensing applies where the property 'is a building in which two or more families/individuals share basic amenities (such as a kitchen or bathroom)' or 'is a converted building which contains one or more units of accommodation that are not self-contained', AND 'It has five or more people (including children) living there', AND 'the five or more people make up more than one household (family unit)'. The national mandatory threshold only. FEE SCHEDULE 2026/27, the council's complete locally-set fee list: HMO Licensing new licence 3-5 units £814.00 Part 1 plus £269.00 Part 2 equals £1,083.00; 6-10 units £904.00 plus £269.00 equals £1,173.00; 11+ units £993.00 plus £269.00 equals £1,262.00; renewal 3-5 units £615.00, 6-10 £660.00, 11+ £705.00; public register requests £6.00 electronic and £9.00 hardcopy; enforcement actions £687.00 each; immigration housing visits £429.00; works in default at cost plus officer time plus a £170 admin fee. The entire locally-set schedule contains mandatory HMO licensing fees only. TRAP: the 'Policy on PSH fees, charges and civil penalties' mentions selective licensing once, at section 2.19, inside a boilerplate list of offences attracting a civil penalty: 'Offences in relation to licensing of houses under part 3 of the Act (selective Licensing) (section 95)'. A recitation of the statutory penalty framework, not a designation. The same policy states at section 1.4 that 'Mid Devon currently has 23 licenced HMOs', consistent with mandatory-only licensing in a rural district, and no licensed non-HMO stock is referenced anywhere. Site searches for 'selective licensing' and 'additional licensing HMO' returned only that policy and the HMO Guidelines 2020, with no designation documents. LIMITATION: the council's search self-describes as covering 'our most popular pages' only, so it is not an exhaustive index; committee papers were not inspected.

notes: No selective or additional licensing. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies (5 or more people). The published licence fee is £578.55, with no discretionary scheme fee. The service is shared with Babergh.
research: The HMO page states: 'All HMOs occupied by five or more people need a licence. It is an offence to operate without a licence.' The national mandatory threshold and nothing further. FEE: 'The fee for a licence is £578.55' - a single mandatory HMO licence fee, with no discretionary scheme fee published. STRONGEST SEARCH NEGATIVE IN THE BATCH: Mid Suffolk's site search accepts URL parameters and honours quoted phrases. A search for the exact phrase 'selective licensing' returned zero results, reported as 'No results were found that matched the keywords: selective licensing'. A search for the exact phrase 'additional licensing' likewise returned zero. A combined search for 'additional licensing' with housing and HMO terms also returned zero. TRAP: an unquoted search for selective licensing returns 144 loose word matches, all general licensing content (Gambling Act 2005, Statement of Licensing Policy, taxis, sexual entertainment venues, Licensing Policy Review) and none housing-related; those counts look like hits but are noise, and only the quoted search is meaningful. SHARED SERVICE: run jointly with Babergh District Council. The HMO page routes applications to a shared Babergh and Mid Suffolk address and publishes 'public registers of issued licenses for both Babergh and Mid Suffolk', and the search index returns joint content, so the zero-result phrase searches cover the shared service. LIMITATION: baberghmidsuffolk.gov.uk itself returned HTTP 503 on repeated attempts and could not be loaded directly; committee papers were not inspected.
